communes: Granja Nova E Vila Chã Da Beira

climate: Seasons this mild ripen Tempranillo, Riesling, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc fully without cooking off their freshness.
Tempranillo sits in its sweet spot, so the wines can show the style it is known for.

soil.rock: Granite weathers to coarse, acid, free-draining soil that warms quickly and holds heat. Its acidity tends to lower the grapes' acidity, which suits Gamay. Schist, slate and gneiss break into stony, free-draining soil that holds the day's heat. Schist is rich in magnesium and potassium but poor in organic matter and nitrogen.
soil.top: The topsoil drains fast and warms early in spring. Vines get little water, which keeps crops small and flavors concentrated, but drought bites hard. It is very acid, which locks up nutrients, so growers spread lime to raise the pH. Stones in it help water drain and store the day's heat, giving it back to the vines at night.

land: The high ground runs about 4°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.
